newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Steel mill shareholder says won Russia rights row.
newsitem.headline: Steel mill shareholder says won Russia rights row.

text.p: Russian investment company Renaissance Capital claimed victory on Thursday in a battle with steelmaker Novolipetsk Metals Combine over shareholder rights.

"The hearing in Lipetsk Regional Arbitration Court ended in a victory for investment company Renaissance Capital in the Novolipetsk Metals Combine shareholder's suit against the enterprise's management," the company said in a statement.

Senior managers at the steel plant were not immediately available for comment. The dispute over the rights of major shareholders to occupy seats on the company's board of directors has highlighted the problems of investing in Russia.

Renaissance, which holds nine percent of shares in the company through its investment arm Sputnik Fund, said the court had ordered the plant to include Renaissance nominees on the list of candidates to the new board of directors.
"I think this is a big victory for Renaissance Capital since at the beginning of this conflict its rights were constantly violated," Renaissance lawyer Konstantin Malofeyev told Reuters.
"The defendant presented no reasons either when it failed to include Renaissance Capital's candidates in the list of nominees to the board of directors or at the hearings."
The court decision follows a ruling last week in favour of Renaissance's fellow shareholder Bank MFK, which owns 15 percent of the plant and was also seeking board representation.
A hearing is scheduled for May 21 in a similar case involving U.S. investment fund Cambridge Capital Management, which owns a 17.2 percent stake in Novolipetsk.
The statement said the court would hear up to six more cases connected with alleged shareholders' rights violations at the steel plant.
